newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair staff vote on wage cut deals.
newsitem.headline: Swissair staff vote on wage cut deals.

text.p: Some 8,500 ground staff at Swissair AG will be voting on its plans to cut salaries and a result is expected in around two weeks, the VPOD union said.
If workers reject the proposals, a neutral mediator will continue negotiations, VPOD said in a statement.
Unions and works councils representing about half of the workers have already agreed on terms with Swissair management, but these must still be ratified by a membership vote.
The other works councils have rejected management's proposals, which aim to reduce personnel costs by about five percent, or around 30 million Swiss francs.
The three works councils that have agreed on terms are Technical, which represents 2,200 employees, Airline, some 1,300 people in administration and Ground Services Geneva.

The works councils that have rejected Swissair's proposals include Ground Services Zurich, which represents 1,400 people, Ground Services Basle, which represents 240 people, Cargo and Logistics, which represents 800 people and Atraxis, which represents 600 people, VPOD said.
VPOD said the main dispute was over the wage reductions, which in some business units exceed the proposed five percent massively.

Last week Swissair announced agreement had been reached by its airline ground staff with the five percent reduction through a three percent wage cut and the remaining two percent through lower payments for irregular working hours, anniversaries and long-service.
In return, Swissair said weekly working hours would be reduced to 41 from 42 and there would be an additional day off during the year.
Swissair has said that wage cuts in Ground Services Zurich will be above-average because wages have to be adjusted to market levels to retain the unit's competitive position.
Swissair is working on improving its bottom line by 500 million francs by the end of 1997, including 100 million in personnel cost through job cuts.
